To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GlcPSe is an electrogenic transporter, but not an electroneutral H+/sugar transporter.
GlcPSe is a sugar transporter that couples sugar and H+ translocation only partially and that this is achieved by a specific arrangement of charged residues in the translocation pathway.

the glucose transporter from S. epidermidis (GlcPSe) is an incomplete H+/sugar carrier, that is, the sugar transport cycle does not depend on the presence of a proton gradient and that the coupling of sugar and proton transport in GlcPSc is incomplete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of residues that are important for the coupling of H+ transport and sugar transport in GlcP.
the question of why GlcPSe is a partially coupled transporter.
the identification of the minimal requirements for electrogenic transport and uncovers an important functional distinction between the two prominent prokaryote GLUT homologs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GlcPSe is a sugar transporter that is able to perform electrogenic transport, but that the coupling between sugar and H+ is incomplete.
the coupling of H+ and sugar transport in GlcP is loose, but not necessarily absent.
the coupling of sugar and proton transport is incomplete in the MFS sugar transporter GlcPSe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GLUT family has a broad range of transport modes, from strictly coupled H+/sugar transporters like XylEEc to partially coupled transporters like GlcPSe to noncoupled H+/sugar antiporters like the human GLUTs, and that the GLUT family is not a monophyletic group.
the coupling of sugar and protons in the major facilitator family is more complex and flexible than previously assumed.
the coupling of sugar and proton translocation is not an inherent property of the MFS but can be tuned by specific amino acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrogenic sugar transport mode is not a universal characteristic of the MFS.
the electrogenic mode of GlcP is not a strict symport, and that this transporter is a valuable model to understand the mechanism of sugar transport and the role of coupling.
the coupling between sugar transport and H+ transport can be incomplete in the MFS, and that the coupling is not a general feature of this transporter family.
